message.content:
Sure! To pull the WHOIS history for **adobe.com** from VirusTotal, you’ll want to hit the “Domain Historical WHOIS” endpoint. Below is a quick example in both `curl` and Python (using the official `requests` library). Just replace `<YOUR_API_KEY>` with your actual key (`adobe_key123` in this case).

---

### 1️⃣ Using `curl`

```bash
curl -X GET \
     -H "x-apikey: <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/adobe.com/whois"
```

> **Tip:**  
> *If you’re on Windows PowerShell, use `Invoke-RestMethod` instead of `curl`.*

---

### 2️⃣ Using Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"
DOMAIN   = "adobe.com"

url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}/whois"
headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
data = response.json()

print(data)          # Pretty‑print or process as needed
```

> **Note:**  
> *Make sure you have `requests` installed (`pip install requests`).*

---

#### What You’ll Get

The JSON payload will contain an array of WHOIS records, each with fields like:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `whois` | Raw WHOIS text |
| `last_update` | Timestamp of the last update |
| `source` | Source database (e.g., ARIN, RIPE) |

You can iterate over `data["data"]` to extract individual entries.

---

### Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Replace `<YOUR_API_KEY>` with your real key. |
| ✅ | Ensure you’re using HTTPS (the URL starts with `https://`). |
| ✅ | Handle pagination if you expect many results (check `data.links.next`). |
| ✅ | Respect VirusTotal’s rate limits (typically 4 requests/minute for free tier). |

That’s all you need to fetch the WHOIS history. Happy querying!
